text:
jordan: Hey — spun up a fresh workspace and followed the node quickstart. First API call returns 403 with message "workspace_not_active". I used a service account key I just created. Anyone run into this?

maria: Can you paste the exact curl / SDK call and the Authorization header (redact the token)?

jordan: sure. curl: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
response: 403 {"error":"workspace_not_active", "msg":"service account not yet propagated"}

sam: Two things to check quickly: 1) how you created the key (UI vs API) and 2) whether your local SDK is caching creds. We've seen a race where the control plane returns 403 for a few seconds after key creation while caches invalidate.

jordan: created via UI > Project > Service accounts > Create key. Did a quick retry after ~10s and still 403.

riley: there's an SDK bug we triaged yesterday — the JS SDK keeps a credential cache file (~/.redwood/cred_cache.json) and doesn't always revalidate when a fresh key appears. If you have that file, try removing it and re-running. Also try explicit auth: `npx @redwood/sdk login --service-key ./my-key.json` to force a fresh token.

jordan: removed the cache file and did `npx @redwood/sdk login --service-key ./sa.json` -> immediate 200. :party: Thanks!

maria: Glad that worked. Can you paste the error log from the failed attempt? I'm trying to reproduce.

jordan: pasted stack snippet from node app: 
```
Error: Request failed with status code 403
    at createError (/app/node_modules/axios/lib/core/createError.js:16:15)
    at settle (/app/node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:17:12)
    at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (/app/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:269:11)
```

sam: That matches the cache-race symptom. We have a small window where the control plane marks the key active but some edge caches still think it's invalid. SDK should retry once after forcing reauth.

devex-bot: Note: internal issue RED-4821 created for credential cache race; assigned to @riley. PR 5823 references a proposed fix.

riley: Yep, PR 5823 (js-sdk) will invalidate cache when 403/workspace_not_active is returned and trigger an immediate reauth. Patch in review; ETA tomorrow. For now, workaround: `rm ~/.redwood/cred_cache.json && npx @redwood/sdk login --service-key ./sa.json` or set env `REDWOOD_DISABLE_AUTH_CACHE=1` if you want to avoid touching files.

maria: Can we add a short note to the quickstart docs: "If you get a 403 on first call after creating a service account, try reauth / clear local cache"? It would save new users some flailing.

sam: I'll raise a tiny docs PR to add that tip and link to the issue. Also adding a short wait + retry in the sample script (3 retries with backoff) is low friction.

jordan: Adding that retry in my sample fixed it for my CI (we had a similar flake in our deploy pipeline). Thanks team. Closing on my side.

maria: Thanks — marking as resolved for now. If the PR lands we'll follow up to remove the workaround note. :thumbsup:
